legend: MARS Dev Team Weekly Report — Legend & Run Notes
Report window: Monday 8/31/2026 – Friday 9/4/2026 (weekdays only). Weekend entries in the worklog (Sat 9/5, Sun 9/6) were not part of this reporting window and are excluded from all totals.
Separate report also produced this run

A separate ad hoc "Cross-Week Flag Summary" workbook (with the optional scoring layer) covering the 4 weeks of 8/3, 8/10, 8/17, and 8/24 was generated alongside this file, per request. It is a standalone deliverable, not a tab in this workbook -- see that file's own About This Report tab for its methodology.
August Month-to-Date tab added this run

This week's Monday (8/31) is the last day of August, and per the plan set at the end of the 8/24-8/30 run ("an Aug 31 stub week was flagged as still remaining before month-end"), this run is where the August close-out happens. The August Month-to-Date tab rolls up: the weeks of 8/3, 8/10, 8/17, 8/24, plus just Monday 8/31 from this week's data (Tue-Fri 9/1-9/4 belong to September and are NOT included in the August MTD tab -- they remain part of this week's Weekly Summary only). I'm treating 8/31 as its own single-day slice for MTD purposes rather than folding in the whole 8/31-9/4 week, since the established plan referred to it as a "stub" -- flagging this assumption in case a different split was intended.

Per spec, Dev Closes and QA Closes are always MTD-scoped regardless of whether the MTD flag tab is built. Now that the MTD tab is included, those two tabs reflect the SAME August 3-31 scope (not just this single week) -- a change from last run, where they were scoped to just that week's activity because the MTD tab was still being deferred.

To keep the whole month internally consistent, I recomputed all 4 prior weeks (8/3, 8/10, 8/17, 8/24) from their raw worklog/PTO/changelog exports using this run's corrected methodology (Offshore Testing as a Testing status, and the dev-owner persistence fix -- see below), rather than reading the numbers back out of the 4 previously-generated report files as-is. Bounce/Low Volume/Low Hours flags in the original 4 files should mostly match (those flags don't depend on either fix), but Dev Closes counts may differ slightly from the originals where the ownership-persistence fix applies.
Two changelog corrections carried over from last run (apply here too)
1. "Offshore Testing" is a Testing status (confirmed by the person running this report).

2. Dev-owner attribution fix: once a dev-owner is genuinely established for a ticket (a real hand-off into testing), that owner persists for its eventual close even if the ticket bounces back to a dev status and closes without re-entering testing -- it did not "skip testing entirely", it just didn't re-enter testing on this pass. The "skips entirely" fallback (crediting whoever is statically assigned at the final row) now only fires when no dev-owner was ever established.
New data-quality items found while processing the 4 prior weeks

• Week of 8/3-8/7: Halina Bobrykava logged 60.0h across 17 distinct tickets on Friday 8/7. No single ticket exceeded the 12h batch-log threshold, so nothing was auto-excluded -- but per spec this is exactly the kind of many-tickets daily total worth flagging for verification with the employee rather than silently accepting. Flagged in her Notes for that week and folded into the MTD Notes.
• Week of 8/10-8/14: Connor Yates logged 23.9h across 7 tickets on Tuesday 8/11. Same situation -- no single ticket over 12h, not auto-excluded, flagged as worth verifying.

• Week of 8/24-8/28: ticket PNP-4715's changelog rows are column-shifted in the source CSV export (an unescaped quote inside the issue summary broke the column alignment) -- same corruption pattern previously seen on MAIN-7987. Both rows for this ticket were skipped rather than parsed incorrectly. Zero impact on anyone's numbers either way, since the ticket's events simply don't get counted.
Data quality flag — elevated unattributed rate, now measured across the full month

Across the full August MTD window (8/3-8/31): 913 distinct tickets reached Done. Of those, 329 (36.0%) could not be attributed to a roster developer and are not counted for anyone; 584 were credited. This week alone (8/31-9/4, shown in the Weekly Summary tab): 235 distinct tickets, 92 unattributed (39.1%), 143 credited.

Bounces, same full MTD window: 248 bounce events were eligible for crediting (after excluding self-moves/automation/instant-reversals). Of those, 107 (43.1%) had no resolvable roster dev-owner; 141 were credited. This week alone: 52 eligible, 27 uncredited (51.9%), 25 credited.

This is a persistent pattern across every week processed this month, not a one-off from this week's export -- so it looks like a real characteristic of this data source rather than a fluke. Tracing examples by hand, two patterns account for it: (1) tickets with real gaps in the middle of their changelog history — e.g. a ticket shows 'Backlog' at creation and then jumps straight to a 'Testing → Done' row much later, with no intermediate hand-off row captured at all; and (2) tickets that resolve to a real assignee who isn't on the MARS roster (QA/PM/other-team names), or to a literal 'Unassigned' state at the hand-off/closure moment. Per the spec, both cases are left unattributed rather than mis-credited — but given how consistent this is across all 5 weeks, it may be worth checking whether the Issue History export process itself is dropping intermediate rows, or whether a meaningful share of this team's tickets are genuinely worked by people outside this roster.
Other assumptions / judgment calls made this run
• Batch-log exclusion: Connor Yates logged 13.1h on PNP-4618 on 8/31, a single ticket/single day >12h. Excluded from his totals per the batch-log rule and flagged in his Notes.
• No day in this window (8/31–9/4) falls on the 2026 holiday schedule, so no holiday adjustments were needed this run.

• I did not find any case this week matching the separate "many tickets, implausible daily total" pattern (the spec's 60h/17-ticket example) — the only >12h single-day total besides the Connor Yates batch log was Allen McAfee at 13.5h across 2 tickets on 9/1, which isn't in the same league and wasn't flagged.
Roster & scope

Only people on the roster (Employees__Hrs_per_Week_Expected.xlsx) are tracked; anyone else who logged time in Jira is ignored. Erin Terre (Staff Engineer) and Halina Bobrykava (Senior Dev) are tracked normally alongside everyone else, per standing project instructions.
Excluded ticket prefixes: PSC, PS, MSP (customer-facing). "MS" (a distinct prefix from "MSP") was kept — those tickets count toward totals.
Hours model & targets

Full workday = 7.5h. Daily logging goal = weekly target ÷ 5. Numeric weekly targets come from each person's own roster value: flat numbers used as-is (Developer/Jr Dev/QA/Other typically 30, Data Engineer 25); ranges use the numeric midpoint for calculations while displaying the range as text (e.g. Senior Dev "15-20" → 17.5 numerically; Staff Engineer "10-15" → 12.5; and the two Developers with an individual "20-30" range → 25).
PTO handling

Every approved timecard row counts as time away from work regardless of Benefit label (PTO, Sick (PTO), Unpaid Time Off, Early Out, Late In, etc.) — this week's PTO file has no Status column, so every row was treated as already-approved. Multi-hour requests are spread across consecutive weekdays (skipping weekends) at 7.5h/day starting at Request Start, jumping forward to the next weekday if Request Start itself falls on a weekend.

Full PTO day (combined logged + PTO ≥ 7.5h that day): cell shows "PTO" (green), no flag, goal → 0; that day's logged hours (if any) are not separately added to the weekly total. Partial PTO day (combined < 7.5h): cell shows logged hours with a trailing *, Notes says "partial PTO day(s)", and that day's goal is reduced proportionally. Hover any PTO-affected cell for the exact hours/benefit breakdown behind it.

This week, Britt Heyward's 37.5h Unpaid-Time-Off request (starting Sat 8/29) spread to land exactly on Mon 8/31–Fri 9/4 — a full PTO week. Jared Rosenthal's 22.5h PTO request (starting Fri 8/28) put Mon 8/31 and Tue 9/1 as full PTO days within this window (Fri 8/28 itself falls outside this report).
Low-logging highlight (daily cell shading + Low Hours Flag)

Daily cells and the Low Hours Flag both compare logged hours against the relevant (PTO/holiday-adjusted) goal: RED < 50%, ORANGE 50–70%, OK > 70%. The Low Hours Flag column uses the full week's prorated target; individual Mon–Fri cells are shaded the same way against that day's own goal.
Low Volume Flag (Developer / Jr Dev / QA only; n/a for Senior Dev, Staff Engineer, Data Engineer, Other)

T = FLOOR(1.5 × full-day-equivalents worked), where full-day-equivalents = prorated period goal ÷ daily goal (so PTO/holiday days count for less than a full day). RED: Tickets Worked ≤ T−2. ORANGE: T−1 to T+1. OK: > T+1. If T ≤ 0 (person out the whole period), flag is OK.
Bounce Flag (Developer / Jr Dev / Senior Dev only; n/a for QA, Staff Engineer, Data Engineer, Other)

A bounce = a ticket moving from a Testing status (Alpha Testing, Alpha Testing (Dev), Alpha Testing (Test), In Testing, Acceptance Testing) back to a Dev status (In Progress, Selected for Development, In Development, Ready, Backlog). Credit always goes to the ticket's dev-owner (whoever it was handed off to before entering testing) — never to the literal actor on the bounce row, who is almost always QA or a PM. Excluded from crediting: self-moves, automation actors, and instant reversals (bounce within the same clock minute as the preceding forward-into-testing move).

Bounce rate = tickets bounced ÷ (tickets worked ∪ any bounced ticket), capped at 100%. The union denominator can exceed the person's own Tickets Worked count if a bounce lands on a ticket they didn't personally log time on this week; both the raw Tickets Worked count and this union denominator are shown (the "n/m" inside the Bounce Rate cell uses the union denominator). HIGH: rate > 25%. WATCH: 15–25%. OK: < 15% (small denominators still flag, e.g. 1/2 = HIGH).
Dev-owner attribution (drives both Bounce credit and Dev Closes)

Credit locks in only at one of two events, using the assignee immediately before that event's own reassignment (walking back through a tight, ≤60-second, status-unchanged, assignee-only row when the hand-off row's own assignee field is static): (1) a real hand-off from a dev-stage status into a testing or publish/staging status, or (2) a ticket that skips testing/publish entirely and goes straight from a dev status to Done. Whoever performs a later, separate release/deploy step is never credited. Tickets where neither event is resolvable in the available history are left unattributed rather than mis-credited — see the data-quality note above for this run's rate.
QA Closes

Credited when a QA's logged time was on a sub-ticket formatted "PARENT-KEY | QA" (e.g. "MAIN-9531: MAIN-9278 | QA") and that parent ticket reached Done in the window. This is necessarily partial — QA testing logged directly on a parent ticket (no sub-ticket) isn't captured. Two other tickets this week contained the text "P3 | QA" in their summary (PROG-345, PROG-346) but "P3" is not a valid parent ticket key, so those were not treated as QA-Closes sub-tickets.
Formulas vs. script-computed values (per xlsx skill)

Wk Total is a live SUM formula over that row's Mon–Fri cells. Bounce Flag, Low Volume Flag, and Low Hours Flag are live IF-formulas referencing their same-row count/rate cells (with each person's goal/threshold/denominator embedded as that row's constant, since those derive from the PTO- and changelog-driven state-machine logic below). Tickets Worked, Bounced, Bounce Rate's underlying counts, and Dev Closes are computed by the reporting script from the worklog and changelog (sequential ticket-history logic that can't reasonably be expressed as in-sheet formulas), per the xlsx skill's documented exception for this kind of count.
Row sort order (Weekly Summary)
Bounce Flag severity (HIGH → WATCH → OK/n/a), then Low Hours Flag severity (RED → ORANGE → OK), then hours logged (Wk Total) descending within each group.
